name: Cursor agent-run control, results and artifact retrieval over the authenticated MCP surface
independence_argument: This route addresses provider-held agent-run state through the cursor-cloud MCP server. It does not traverse GitHub, does not use the git protocol and does not depend on any repository credential. R1 traverses GitHub over HTTPS with a separate identity. Either route can fail without disabling the other.

bounded_work_unit.description: Initiate one bounded provider-side retrieval job for a single addressable agent run and collect its result artifacts.
bounded_work_unit.scope_control: Addressed only this orchestrator's own run id. PO-03 parent threads were deliberately not opened, fetched or monitored, as the launch sheet requires.

result_retrieval.addressing_scheme: provider run id (bcId) -> run directory -> per-run artifact files
result_retrieval.ephemerality_note: The provider run directory is VM-local and non-durable. The retrieved content is therefore reconciled into the repository under receipts/so02/** where the hash-bound bundle, not the provider path, is canonical.

additional_control_operations_proved.returns: own run identity, stable agent URL, exact model, owner, lifecycle status
addressable enumeration of all 9 visible top-level runs with per-run status; this is the instrument used for PO-03 capacity observation
environment public id, environment build id, egress policy, repository binding

stable_locators.resume_checkpoint: bcId=bc-c6f63d58-9611-495a-96f6-2f2dcbef696d; resume by addressing the run id through cursor-cloud run-info or batch-fetch-details

failure_injection.injected: batch-fetch-details addressed to a well-formed but non-existent run id bc-00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
failure_injection.observed: Fetched 0 available cloud agent(s); the tool named the unavailable id explicitly and wrote no agent artifact.

limits_and_honest_gaps: This route exposes agent-run observation, artifact retrieval and environment control. It does not, in this runtime, expose creation of a new top-level agent run or submission of a follow-up to another run; that remains an owner or REST-API action (see R4A).
The provider run directory is not durable across VMs, so the route cannot be canonical on its own.
